title: Redis outage masked as a cache miss — degradation policy silently bypassed
expected_feedback: Critical: `err != nil` collapses two states that require opposite responses. A miss (redis.Nil) should populate the cache; an outage (dial timeout, CLUSTERDOWN, connection-pool exhaustion) must trip the degradation path. Because they are merged, a Redis outage converts the full 40k QPS into direct DB traffic with no rate limit, no singleflight, and no circuit breaker — the cache layer's own degradation policy is bypassed at exactly the moment it is needed, and the DB fails second. Two further defects compound it: the repopulating SET is issued against the Redis that is already down and its error is discarded, and expiration 0 means any entry written during a partial outage never expires. Fix: branch on errors.Is(err, redis.Nil) for the populate path; treat every other error as ErrCacheUnavailable and route it through the documented degradation path (rate-limited DB fallback or degraded response); give the populate a bounded, jittered TTL.
violated_rule: Cache-down degradation path exists and is distinguishable from a miss
detector_note: The headline defect (outage conflated with miss) is a control-flow judgement no regex reliably gates; the two compounding defects are gated. Listed so the gap is data, not silence.
